title: What the State tax-credit rules say about San Francisco’s share and tie-breaks
question: Do the State tax-credit regulations’ set-asides, regional shares and tie-breakers explain the San Francisco applications the scored-rounds screen found passed over?
finding: Not the two that were found: both (2022, applications of August 9, 2025, applications of May 20) were bond rounds, which the regulations hand to the Debt Limit Allocation Committee's own scoring (its Regulation 5106, not on disk). For the 9% rounds the regulations give San Francisco a 3.7% regional share and make a letter from the Mayor's Office of Housing the first tie-breaker among San Francisco applications; in the 9% rounds with an award list 9 of 11 San Francisco applications were funded and none was passed over.
how: Text of the December 2025 regulations and the 2026 version (with changes marked), read with pdftotext; each rule shown was checked to appear in the text. Set against the scored-rounds screen in the site’s “Drawings and repeat winners” page.
limits: The 2026 file shows deleted and added words run together, so only rules whose text survives intact are cited from it. The Debt Limit Allocation Committee regulations, which govern the bond rounds, are not on disk; until they are, the two passed-over rows stay questions. Staff reports for each round would say why a given application was not funded.

columns.t: What it means for San Francisco

rows.says: San Francisco County gets about 3.7% of the yearly federal and State 9% credit ceiling (3.7% in the 2026 text).
rows.bearing: San Francisco 9% applications compete mainly with each other for a small share: in the rounds with an award list, 9 of 11 San Francisco applications were funded; the two that were not scored 99 and 98 against 109 for funded ones.
rows.explains: Explains why San Francisco usually wins about one 9% award a round; no 9% application was found passed over.

rows.rule: First tie-breaker in San Francisco: a letter from the Mayor’s Office of Housing
rows.says: For the San Francisco and Los Angeles apportionments the first tie-breaker is a formal letter of support from the San Francisco Mayor’s Office of Housing (Los Angeles: its housing department); same text in 2026.
rows.bearing: Among San Francisco 9% applications with equal points, a City office decides the order by issuing or withholding a letter. The regulation provides for this; it means City preference, not only the State formula, settles close calls.

rows.says: An application whose housing type has met its goal in the round is skipped in a tie; goal percentages include Large Family 65%, Special Needs 40%, At-Risk 15%, Seniors 20%.
rows.bearing: A lower-scored project of an under-served type can be funded before an equal-scored one.

rows.rule: Bond-financed (4%) projects are scored by the Debt Limit Allocation Committee
rows.says: Tax-exempt bond projects are competitively scored under the California Debt Limit Allocation Committee's own regulations (Section 5106), not these.
rows.bearing: Both San Francisco applications the scored-rounds screen counts as passed over (Balboa Reservoir Building E (2022, applications of August 9); 399 5th Street (2025, applications of May 20)) were in bond rounds, so these regulations cannot explain them; the Committee's regulations, its pool and set-aside rules and its tie-breaker (a public-benefit ratio) would, and they are not on disk.
rows.explains: Does not explain the passed-over rows.
